rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance. This experiment tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, clarifying whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines. It addresses the critical design choice of fusion strategy (concat vs weighted) and modalities, providing foundational insights before exploring more complex configurations.

The existing evidence from config_016 (validation accuracy 0.5266) shows that multimodal singleprofile with pca_n2000 and resnet50 using concat fusion performs moderately. This experiment tests the impact of changing the fusion method from concat to weighted, a critical design choice in multimodal models. It directly extends the previous configuration, reducing uncertainty about whether fusion strategy significantly affects performance, while balancing exploitation of the current promising multimodal direction.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) with the same encoders, clarifying whether profile setting (single vs multi) is a critical factor. It balances exploration of a key design choice (profile setting) while building on prior multimodal success, avoiding redundant singleprofile tests.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile and multimodal settings yield higher accuracy (config_018: 0.618). This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted (config_019) improves performance for multiprofile multimodal models. It clarifies the impact of fusion methods in this context, which is critical for optimizing design choices without overinterpreting small differences in prior experiments.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high validation accuracy (0.639 in config_019). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) maintains or improves performance, clarifying the impact of RNA encoder choice. This is a critical design decision with potential for significant performance gains, and it avoids repeating prior configurations while building on the promising multimodal multiprofile framework.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder (while keeping avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion) further improves performance. This clarifies the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong evidence from config_031 to explore a logical extension.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA and image encoders and weighted fusion, clarifying whether transformer aggregation improves performance further. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of aggregation methods, which are critical for multimodal integration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989 in config_039). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt, which may improve performance further. It clarifies whether the more advanced scgpt encoder provides additional benefits when combined with the already effective transformer aggregation and weighted fusion strategy. This is the best use of the next experiment as it builds on a proven successful configuration while exploring a critical design choice (RNA encoder).

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same components clarifies the impact of fusion type. It is the best use of the next experiment as it explores a key design choice (fusion method) that could influence performance, while building on the promising direction of scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_039) yield high accuracy, but there is uncertainty about whether avgpool aggregation could be beneficial with scgpt RNA encoder. This experiment tests scgpt with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, clarifying the impact of aggregation method on performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (aggregation) while building on the success of scgpt and weighted fusion.
